podcast.title: 2024 Reunion Chatter
podcast.body: In April 2024, a video surfaced on Instagram showing all five Spice Girls reunited at Victoria Beckham's 50th birthday party, spontaneously singing "Mama." This fueled speculation among fans about a potential reunion and tour, highlighting a continued yearning for the group despite decades of inactivity. "As we were preparing this hit parade episode in April 2024, a video appeared on Instagram of the five members of the Spice Girls reunited at the 50th birthday party of Posh Spice, Victoria Beckham."

podcast.title: Ditching Original Management and Signing with Virgin
podcast.body: By 1995, the group ditched their original management team, feeling their ideas weren't being heard. They retained their songwriters, found new producers, and secured Simon Fuller as their manager. They signed with Virgin Records, which notably agreed to let them present themselves as five equal personalities with no single lead singer. "By 1995, the future Spice Girls had ditched the management team who had auditioned them out of concern that they weren't listening to the ladies' ideas."

podcast.title: Formation and Early Management
podcast.body: The group was formed in 1994 after London managers held auditions to find a girl group to compete with British boy bands, using Eternal's "Stay" as the audition song. After some member changes, Victoria Adams, Melanie Brown, Emma Bunton, Melanie Chisholm, and Geri Halliwell were chosen. Initially called "Touch," they briefly adopted "Spice" before settling on "Spice Girls" due to another rapper named Spice. "At first they were called Touch. Then, after working on a song called Sugar and Spice, they went with Spice as a moniker. Eventually, after learning that there already was a rapper called Spice, they would settle on the Spice Girls."

podcast.title: Press-Given Nicknames
podcast.body: The distinct nicknames for each member — Baby Spice (Emma Bunton), Posh Spice (Victoria Adams), Scary Spice (Melanie Brown), Sporty Spice (Melanie Chisholm), and Ginger Spice (Geri Halliwell) — were given by the press, not self-chosen. The slogan "Girl Power" was also not their invention, but they heartily embraced both as essential to their brand. "Press gave the five ladies new nicknames. Emma was now called Baby Spice. Victoria was nicknamed Posh Spice. Mel B was dubbed Scary Spice. Mel C Sporty Spice. And the red-haired Jerry became Ginger Spice."

xref.title: Vocals on World Cup Theme Song
xref.body: A song originally from the unreleased collaboration between Ian McCulloch and Johnny Marr ended up being used as a World Cup theme song, featuring vocals from The Spice Girls. This unexpected use of the track provided a different outlet for some of the material from the reportedly stolen album. "And another ended up as a World Cup theme song with vocals from The Spice Girls."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
